title: a whole-suite intent-cli run reds one daemon ingest arm that passes alone, against a 96-second budget
body:
`sync_to_disk_runs_beside_a_watching_daemon::sync_to_disk_lands_beside_a_watching_daemon_and_costs_it_no_ingest` (native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/sync_to_disk_runs_beside_a_watching_daemon.rs:92) fails in a whole-crate `cargo test -p intent-cli` run and passes when run alone. The panic is `the daemon ingested the sentinel: not seen within 4800 tries`.

THE BUDGET IS WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN SHRUGGED AT. `ARM_ATTEMPTS` is `ATTEMPTS * 12` (:35), `ATTEMPTS` is 400 and `PAUSE` is 20ms (intent-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:145,147), so the bound is NINETY-SIX SECONDS of wall clock for the daemon to ingest one sentinel. "The box was busy" is a thin explanation for missing a bound that loose, and a daemon-family red on this host is ruled to be judged by RATE at the FLOOR rather than by any single verdict. So the hypothesis is not free and the verdict is PARKED rather than taken.

MEASURED SO FAR, 2026-09-22, four runs:

- whole-suite `-p intentsvcs -p intent-cli`, load 29 at start: PASSED
- whole-suite `-p intentsvcs -p intent-cli`, load ~25: FAILED
- isolated, the one test alone, load ~18-22: PASSED in 7.13s
- whole-suite `-p intent-cli`, load ~25-27: FAILED
- whole-suite `-p intent-cli`, load 18.28 before and 16.93 after: FAILED

The last one matters most and it cuts AGAINST the contention hypothesis: the same red at the lowest starting load of the set. The 5-minute average during it was 24.69, and the suite's own 741-test parallelism is what produces that -- which is the point. A box "clear" of other nodes is not a box clear of this suite, so clearing the host does not by itself relieve the contention this test competes with.

WHAT THE DECISIVE RUN MUST DISTINGUISH (vc, 2026-09-22): if it REDS with the host at the floor, the budget is not the story and there is a daemon regression to find. If it GREENS at the floor, the finding is that 741 tests of parallel contention can starve a 96-second budget -- which is itself worth recording, because it bounds every other daemon arm in this suite and not just this one.

NOT CAUSED BY 0509, and the argument is the shape rather than the conclusion so a reader who has not seen that diff can check it: 0509's whole change is `Report::unclaimed_digest` plus its single call site inside `render_organize_report`. To reach either, this test would have to render an organize report. It never does -- the strings `organize`, `unclaimed` and `digest` do not appear anywhere in the test file. `intentsvcs`, the crate the change lives in, is fully green at RC=0 with 1528 passed and 4 ignored across the same runs.

SUPERSEDES THE PARKING CONDITION ABOVE (vc, 2026-09-22, after cc's third run). "Wait until the box is clear" is NOT the decisive condition and nobody should wait on it. The third run red at the lowest starting load of the set, and the suite's own 741-test parallelism is what produces the contention, so a host cleared of every other node is still not a cleared box for this test. The corpus rule about re-running a daemon-family red AT THE FLOOR cannot settle this one, because the floor is not the variable.

WHAT WOULD DISCRIMINATE, and either arm is enough: run this test's file ALONE under a synthetic parallel load, or run the whole `intent-cli` suite with reduced test-threads. Both separate "starved by 741 neighbours" from "daemon regression", which no amount of waiting for a quiet host can do. If it reds with the neighbours removed, the budget is not the story and there is a regression to find. If it greens, the finding is that this suite's own parallelism can starve a 96-second budget -- which bounds every other daemon arm in the suite and not just this one.

A NATURAL EXPERIMENT, UNPLANNED, AND THE FIRST EVIDENCE THAT SEPARATES THE TWO BRANCHES (cc, 2026-09-22 16:40Z). The same `cargo test -p intent-cli`, same machine, same binary, run once more with the box effectively uncontended after two peers released it:

    with two peers' work live ....... 126.46s, 1 red (this arm)
    box effectively clear ...........  34.19s, 0 red, RC=0, 742 passed

FOUR TIMES FASTER AND THE RED IS GONE. This is not the synthetic-load or reduced-test-threads run named above, and it does not demonstrate a mechanism -- it is an observation over two uncontrolled conditions, and the confound is that the whole machine differed, not just this suite's neighbours. But it is the first measurement whose two arms fall on opposite sides of the question, and it points at STARVED BY NEIGHBOURS rather than at a daemon regression.

What it adds beyond the earlier five runs is the TIMING, which none of them recorded and which is the variable that actually matters: a suite taking 126s to do what it can do in 34s is spending three quarters of its time waiting, and this arm's budget is consumed by exactly that waiting. It also supersedes, gently, the reading that the suite's own parallelism is sufficient to starve the arm -- the suite's own parallelism was present in BOTH conditions, so whatever made the difference came from OUTSIDE the suite. That weakens the "clearing the box cannot help" argument this body makes above, which was reasoned rather than measured, and the measurement is better than the reasoning.

The discriminating runs named above are still owed. This one narrows where to look; it does not close it.

THE CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS THE TIMING PAIR, AND IT IS WORSE THAN AN UNVERIFIED CONDITION (cc, on vc's catch). "Box effectively clear" was established over the INTENT ROSTER ONLY -- the heavy-run protocol coordinates four nodes and the box is a machine. ic found both its judging runs sat start to finish inside a Devbin bats window, a different estate on the same host, while all four Intent nodes read idle by the protocol's own reckoning; vc then confirmed the class live, counting 56 Devbin bats processes at a moment when nothing of Intent's was running.

FOR THIS PAIR SPECIFICALLY THE FAILURE IS NOT THAT THE CONDITION WAS UNMEASURED. It was measured. Immediately before the 34.19s run, `ps -axo args= | grep -c '[b]ats'` read 13, with `devbin test bats`, `releasecut.bats` and a log named `20260922-1625.bats.out` among them, and the run was started anyway on the reasoning that cargo and bats are different populations. That reasoning may even be right, but it was never the claim: the claim the number carries is that one condition was quiet and the other was not, and the quiet one demonstrably was not quiet. The measurement existed and did not reach the conclusion drawn from it.

SO WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT. The RED APPEARING IN ONE CONDITION AND NOT THE OTHER survives -- foreign load cannot turn a red green, and it remains the first observation whose arms fall on opposite sides. THE FOUR-TIMES FIGURE DOES NOT survive as a contention ratio, because the denominator condition was unmeasured as to the machine and the numerator condition is now known to have carried foreign load of unknown size. Read 126.46s against 34.19s as two timings taken under two differently-contended conditions, neither of them characterised.

THE CENSUS THAT ANSWERS WHAT THE PROTOCOL CANNOT (vc), for whoever takes the discriminating runs:

    ps -axo args= | grep -E '[b]ats-exec|[c]argo test|[r]ustc' | grep -oE '/Users/matts/Devel/prj/[A-Za-z_]+' | sort | uniq -c

It names the ESTATE each heavy process belongs to. Announce to the roster as now, then census the MACHINE, and state which of the two was verified. A delta between two runs under one constant confound needs neither; a TIMING needs the machine.

THE FOREIGN WINDOW, MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED, AND IT FALLS THE OTHER WAY FROM BOTH GUESSES (cc, 2026-09-22T16:47:43Z from `date -u`). `ps -axo lstart=,args=` gives Devbin's suite a single start: `bash .../bats-core/bats tests/unit`, launched by `bin/devbin test bats`, at 17:25:07 LOCAL = 16:25:07Z, still alive when this was written twenty-two minutes later. That is one window with a known start, not a guess.

Laid against this issue's own runs:

    ~16:09Z  whole-suite       intent-cli PASSED      before the window
    ~16:14Z  whole-suite       intent-cli FAILED      before the window
     16:17Z  the arm alone     PASSED in 7.13s        before the window
    ~16:22Z  whole-suite       intent-cli FAILED      before the window
    ~16:25Z  whole-suite       intent-cli FAILED      ends as the window opens
     16:40Z  whole-suite       PASSED, 34.19s         INSIDE the window

SO EVERY RED PREDATES THE FOREIGN SUITE AND THE ONLY GREEN SITS INSIDE IT. The suggestion that both conditions sat inside one constant foreign window -- which would have made this a controlled comparison with the confound held fixed by accident -- is not what the process table says. The two conditions differ in TWO ways at once and in OPPOSITE directions: the red runs carried Intent's own peers and no Devbin, the green run carried Devbin and no Intent peers.

WHICH MAKES THE TIMING PAIR WEAKER AS A CONTENTION RATIO AND SHARPER AS A POINTER. Weaker, because two variables moved and the faster run was the one with MORE foreign load, so no ratio can be read off it. Sharper, because if more foreign load coincided with a four-times FASTER suite and no red, then the foreign estate is not the variable that matters here and INTENT'S OWN CONCURRENT NODES are the candidate -- which is a narrower hypothesis than "contention" and a different one from "this suite's own 741-test parallelism", since that was constant across all six runs.

NOTHING HERE IS CONTROLLED AND NONE OF IT DEMONSTRATES A MECHANISM. Six observations under six uncharacterised conditions, with the timing recorded for only two of them. It is recorded because the correlation runs opposite to the obvious reading, and an opposite-running correlation is the cheapest thing to lose and the most expensive to re-derive.
